Subject: Proposed demo cadence & overlapping windows (AE+SE+Eng+Procurement)

Hi Alejandro / FinTech procurement,

Thanks again for the quick discovery call earlier. We want to lock in a demo that gives your engineers a deep look at the integration flow (30–45 min demo + 15–30 min Q&A) while making sure SE + AE are in the room to address infra/ops and pricing questions. Given your teams in Madrid/London and our teams split across SF and Berlin, I sketched a rotating schedule to hit a fair overlap for US/EU/APAC customers.

Attached is a simple availability matrix (availability_matrix.csv) showing our team windows across timezones. I also started a quick poll here: https://doodle.com/poll/rotating-slots-xyz and a shared sheet for any edits: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1abcdExampleAvail

Quick ask: can you confirm who from your side will attend (Engineer + Security + Procurement) and any absolute blackout windows (e.g., no meetings before 10:00 CET or after 18:00 CET)? That will help me propose three concrete slots we can rotate on a weekly cadence (week A: US-friendly, week B: EU-friendly, week C: APAC-friendly).

Proposed demo length: 60–75 minutes. SE will demo an end-to-end inferencing flow + KV cache behavior; AE will cover price/commit options and Dedicated/Private variants. If procurement needs a PO or specific docs before the call, please flag.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with concrete slot options once I have your constraints.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Hi Rishi — thanks. I’m the lead engineer for the integration (Madrid office).

High-level constraints from engineering/security:
- Best overlap is 09:30–11:30 CET or 15:00–17:00 CET on weekdays (we have core deploy windows after 17:30 CET).
- We prefer demos that start no earlier than 09:30 CET to avoid deep work disruption.
- Security would like a short (10 min) segment to talk about data residency and audit logs; Liu Chen (cc’d) can join for that.

Procurement: I’ll defer to them for timing around PO/NDA. For planning, assume the attendees will be: Alejandro Ruiz (Eng), Liu Chen (Security), and Procurement Team (procurement@fintechco.com).

If possible, can you propose 3 slots that fall in our 09:30–11:30 or 15:00–17:00 CET windows, and call out which ones are US-friendly / EU-friendly / APAC-friendly for rotation planning?

Thanks — Alejandro

Thanks for the context Alejandro — quick technical notes and a few concrete timing options from the SE side.

Technical: we need ~60 minutes to demo Dedicated routing, KV cache warm-up behavior, and an infra failover scenario. If you want the security segment, we can slot a 10-minute security walkthrough mid-demo (recommended right after the live inference run so logs/retention talk maps directly to the example).

Timing options (all converted to CET for clarity; I’ve noted how they map to Redwood team timezones):
- Option A (EU-friendly): Tue 12 May, 15:30–16:45 CET — US teams: 06:30–07:45 PT (early), APAC: 22:30–23:45 SGT (late)
- Option B (US-friendly): Wed 13 May, 09:30–10:45 CET — US teams: 03:30–04:45 PT (very early) — not ideal for AE in SF unless rotating week
- Option C (balanced rotation): Thu 14 May, 08:30–09:45 CET — US teams: 00:30–01:45 PT (overnight), APAC: 15:30–16:45 SGT (good)

Recommendation: pick Option A for the first EU-week demo (good overlap for FinTech engineering), then rotate to an APAC-friendly slot the following week (so the SF AE covers an earlier week). If procurement requests daytime CET slots consistently, we can shift the rotation cadence to bi-weekly.

I’ll prepare a short runbook and the demo deck; Rishi, if you confirm attendees I’ll tailor the security segment to Liu’s questions.

—Jonas
